source.text: Περὶ μὲν γὰρ τῆς διακονίας τῆς εἰς τοὺς ἁγίους περισσόν μοί ἐστιν τὸ γράφειν ὑμῖν, οἶδα γὰρ τὴν προθυμίαν ὑμῶν ἣν ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν καυχῶμαι Μακεδόσιν ὅτι Ἀχαΐα παρεσκεύασται ἀπὸ πέρυσι, καὶ τὸ ὑμῶν ζῆλος ἠρέθισε τοὺς πλείονας.

records.literal_gloss: Concerning indeed for the ministry the [one] for the holy ones superfluous for me it is the to write to you, \v 2 I know for the readiness of you which on behalf of you I boast to Macedonians that Achaia has been prepared from last year, and the of you zeal stirred up the more.

en.L: For concerning the ministry for the holy ones, it is superfluous for me to write to you, \v 2 for I know your readiness, which I boast of on your behalf to [the] Macedonians, [saying] that Achaia has been prepared since last year; and your zeal has stirred up most of them.
en.B: There is really no need for me to write to you about the relief for God's holy people. \v 2 I know how willing you are, and I speak of it with pride to the Macedonians: "Achaia has been ready since last year." Your zeal has spurred most of them into action.
en.R: I do not really need to write to you about helping God's people in Jerusalem. \v 2 I know that you want to help. I keep telling the believers in Macedonia how proud I am of you. I tell them, "The believers in Achaia have been ready to give since last year." And your eagerness has made most of them eager too.

fr.L: Car au sujet du ministère en faveur des saints, il est superflu pour moi de vous écrire, \v 2 car je connais votre empressement, dont je me vante à votre sujet auprès des Macédoniens, [disant] que l’Achaïe est prête depuis l’an dernier ; et votre zèle a stimulé la plupart d’entre eux.
fr.B: Il est vraiment inutile que je vous écrive au sujet du secours destiné au peuple saint de Dieu. \v 2 Je sais combien vous êtes bien disposés, et j’en parle avec fierté aux Macédoniens : « L’Achaïe est prête depuis l’an dernier. » Votre zèle a poussé la plupart d’entre eux à agir.
fr.R: Je n’ai pas vraiment besoin de vous écrire au sujet de l’aide pour le peuple de Dieu à Jérusalem. \v 2 Je sais que vous voulez aider. Je ne cesse de dire aux croyants de Macédoine combien je suis fier de vous. Je leur dis : « Les croyants d’Achaïe sont prêts à donner depuis l’an dernier. » Et votre empressement a rendu la plupart d’entre eux empressés eux aussi.

es.L: Porque en cuanto al ministerio para los santos, me es superfluo {{plural_you:escribirles|escribiros}}, \v 2 porque conozco {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} buena disposición, de la cual me glorío ante [los] macedonios a favor de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, [diciendo] que Acaya está preparada desde el año pasado; y el celo de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ha estimulado a la mayoría [de ellos].
es.B: No hace falta que {{plural_you:les|os}} escriba acerca de la ayuda para el pueblo santo de Dios. \v 2 Conozco {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} buena disposición, y hablo de ella con orgullo a los macedonios: «Acaya está preparada desde el año pasado». El celo de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ha movido a la mayoría de ellos a actuar.
es.R: En realidad no hace falta que {{plural_you:les|os}} escriba sobre la ayuda para el pueblo de Dios en Jerusalén. \v 2 Sé que {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} ayudar. Siempre les digo a los creyentes de Macedonia lo orgulloso que estoy de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Les digo: «Los creyentes de Acaya están listos para dar desde el año pasado». Y el entusiasmo de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} ha hecho que la mayoría de ellos también quiera ayudar.

decisions.choice: for: chapter 9 goes on from the end of chapter 8
alternatives: a separate letter about the collection, later joined to chapter 8
decisions.reason: μὲν γὰρ ties this sentence to what comes before: Paul has just asked the Corinthians to welcome the brothers he is sending (8:16-24), and now he explains that they come about the collection. Some have argued that chapter 9 was once a separate note, since it speaks of the collection as if for the first time, but the words "the brothers" in verse 3 assume that the reader knows who they are from chapter 8.

decisions.choice: the collection for the poor believers in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: As in 8:4, διακονίας is the relief fund Paul was gathering from his Gentile churches for the poor among the believers in Jerusalem (Romans 15:25-27; 1 Corinthians 16:1-4). "The holy ones" are the believers in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Achaia: the Roman province of southern Greece, with Corinth as its capital
decisions.reason: Paul names the province, as in 1:1, to take in the church at Corinth and the believers around it. He is writing from Macedonia, the province to the north (8:1), and he holds up each province as an example to the other: Achaia's early readiness stirred up Macedonia (here), and Macedonia's generous giving is now held up to Achaia (8:1-5).

decisions.choice: stirred up: spurred others on, in a good sense
decisions.reason: ἠρέθισε can mean to provoke or exasperate, as in Colossians 3:21, but here the zeal of the Corinthians moved the Macedonians to act. πλείονας means "the greater number": most of the Macedonian believers.

decisions.choice: boast: Paul's proud confidence in the Corinthians
decisions.reason: καυχῶμαι is good pride here, the same boasting about the Corinthians as in 7:14 and 8:24. The present tense shows that Paul is still speaking of them this way in Macedonia as he writes.

decisions.choice: what Paul says to the Macedonians: Achaia has been ready since last year
decisions.reason: ὅτι gives the content of Paul's boast, almost his very words. "Since last year" matches 8:10. "Ready" means ready in their eagerness to give; verses 3-5 show that the money itself had still to be gathered.

decisions.choice: ministry (L); relief (B); helping (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for the collection, as in 8:4: "ministry" alone would make readers think of preaching (m2).

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of this word.

decisions.choice: boast (L); speak of it with pride (B); how proud I am (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide choice: Literal keeps "boast" so the word can be traced; Balanced and Readable speak of pride, since this is good pride and the argument does not turn on the word itself (m5).

decisions.choice: in Jerusalem; the believers in Macedonia; the believers in Achaia ... to give
decisions.reason: Readable says who the holy ones were and that the provinces stand for the believers in them, and names what Achaia was ready to do (m2, m3, m6).

decisions.choice: le ministère (L), le secours (B), l’aide (R); je me vante (L), j’en parle avec fierté (B), je suis fier (R), as in chapter 8
decisions.reason: The same words as in 8:4 and 7:4 for the collection and for Paul's good pride in the church, so that chapter 9 reads as the continuation of chapter 8. Literal says "se vanter", the one word for boasting across 1 and 2 Corinthians (1:12; docs/corinthians-terms.md).

decisions.choice: me glorío (L); hablo de ella con orgullo (B); lo orgulloso que estoy (R)
decisions.reason: As in 1:12 and 8:24: Literal keeps "gloriarse" so the boasting word can be traced; in chapters 8-9 Paul's boasting is proper pride in the Corinthians (meaning decision), so Balanced and Readable say "orgullo", as the English does.

decisions.choice: ministerio (L); la ayuda (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:4: the service word names the collection for Jerusalem, and "ministerio" alone would suggest preaching, so Balanced and Readable say "la ayuda".

source.text: ἔπεμψα δὲ τοὺς ἀδελφούς, ἵνα μὴ τὸ καύχημα ἡμῶν τὸ ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν κενωθῇ ἐν τῷ μέρει τούτῳ, ἵνα καθὼς ἔλεγον παρεσκευασμένοι ἦτε, μή πως ἐὰν ἔλθωσιν σὺν ἐμοὶ Μακεδόνες καὶ εὕρωσιν ὑμᾶς ἀπαρασκευάστους καταισχυνθῶμεν ἡμεῖς, ἵνα μὴ λέγωμεν ὑμεῖς, ἐν τῇ ὑποστάσει ταύτῃ.

records.literal_gloss: I sent and the brothers, so that not the boast of us the [one] about you be emptied in the matter this, so that just as I was saying prepared you may be, \v 4 lest perhaps if come with me Macedonians and find you unprepared be put to shame we, that not we say you, in the confidence this.

en.L: But I am sending the brothers, so that our boasting about you may not be made empty in this matter, so that you may be prepared, just as I was saying; \v 4 lest perhaps, if Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we be put to shame (not to say you) in this confidence.
en.B: The reason I am sending the brothers is so that our pride in you does not prove hollow on this point, and so that you are ready, as I kept saying you would be. \v 4 Otherwise, if some Macedonians travel with me and discover that you are not ready, we would be put to shame for having been so confident, to say nothing of you.
en.R: I am sending these brothers to you because I do not want it to turn out that we were wrong to be proud of you. I want you to be ready, just as I said you would be. \v 4 Some people from Macedonia may come with me. If they find that you are not ready, we will be ashamed that we were so sure of you. And you will be even more ashamed!

fr.L: Mais j’envoie les frères, afin que notre sujet de fierté à votre égard ne soit pas rendu vain sur ce point, afin que vous soyez prêts, comme je le disais, \v 4 de peur que, si des Macédoniens viennent avec moi et vous trouvent non préparés, nous ne soyons couverts de honte (pour ne pas dire vous) dans cette assurance.
fr.B: Si j’envoie les frères, c’est pour que notre fierté à votre sujet ne se révèle pas sans fondement sur ce point, et pour que vous soyez prêts, comme je n’ai cessé de le dire. \v 4 Sinon, si des Macédoniens viennent avec moi et découvrent que vous n’êtes pas prêts, nous serions couverts de honte d’avoir été si confiants, pour ne rien dire de vous.
fr.R: J’envoie ces frères chez vous parce que je ne veux pas qu’il apparaisse que nous avions tort d’être fiers de vous. Je veux que vous soyez prêts, comme je l’ai dit. \v 4 Des gens de Macédoine viendront peut-être avec moi. S’ils découvrent que vous n’êtes pas prêts, nous aurons honte d’avoir été si sûrs de vous. Et vous aurez encore plus honte !

es.L: Pero envío a los hermanos para que nuestro motivo de gloria acerca de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no quede vacío en este asunto, para que, como yo decía, {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} preparados; \v 4 no sea que, si vienen conmigo macedonios y {{plural_you:los|os}} encuentran desprevenidos, nosotros (por no decir {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}) seamos avergonzados en esta confianza.
es.B: Envío a los hermanos para que el orgullo que sentimos por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} no resulte vano en este punto, y para que {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} preparados, como yo he venido diciendo. \v 4 De lo contrario, si algunos macedonios viajan conmigo y {{plural_you:los|os}} encuentran sin preparar, nosotros quedaríamos avergonzados por haber estado tan seguros, por no hablar de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} envío a estos hermanos porque no quiero que resulte que nos equivocamos al sentirnos orgullosos de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. Quiero que {{plural_you:estén|estéis}} preparados, tal como dije que {{plural_you:lo estarían|lo estaríais}}. \v 4 Puede que algunas personas de Macedonia vengan conmigo. Si ven que no {{plural_you:están|estáis}} preparados, nosotros sentiremos vergüenza por haber estado tan seguros de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}. ¡Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} {{plural_you:sentirán|sentiréis}} todavía más vergüenza!

decisions.choice: I am sending: the brothers travel with this letter
decisions.reason: ἔπεμψα is past in form, but letter writers often wrote from the point of view of the reader, for whom the sending had already happened, as in 8:17-18 and 8:22. "The brothers" are Titus and the two men of 8:18-22.

decisions.choice: boast: Paul's proud claims about the Corinthians, which could be shown to be empty
decisions.reason: καύχημα is the thing Paul has boasted of, his good pride in them (verse 2). κενωθῇ means to be made empty: if the Corinthians are not ready, his words about them will turn out to have nothing behind them. "In this matter" limits the point to the collection; Paul's pride in them on other matters stands (7:4, 14).

decisions.choice: confidence: Paul's assurance about the Corinthians
decisions.reason: ὑποστάσει can mean confidence or assurance, as in 11:17 and Hebrews 3:14, and it can also mean a plan or undertaking. Since Paul has just spoken of his boasting, "confidence" fits best: he would be ashamed of having been so sure of them. The other sense, "in this undertaking", is also possible.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: "in this confidence"
alternatives: many later manuscripts add "of boasting": "in this confident boasting"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, add a word for "boasting" after "this confidence", which makes the link with verse 3 explicit. The older manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: a tactful aside: the shame would really be the Corinthians'
decisions.reason: ἵνα μὴ λέγωμεν ὑμεῖς means "so that we do not say: you". Paul speaks of his own shame but lets the readers see that the greater shame would be theirs, the church that promised and did not deliver.

decisions.choice: Macedonian believers who might travel with Paul to Corinth
decisions.reason: Representatives of the churches went with the collection to Jerusalem (8:19, 23; 1 Corinthians 16:3-4), and Acts 20:4 names men from Berea and Thessalonica who traveled with Paul. Some of them might come through Corinth with him.

decisions.choice: I am sending
decisions.reason: English says "I am sending" for a letter writer's past tense of sending, as in 8:17-18 (m1). "The brothers" takes no gender span: they are particular men.

decisions.choice: boasting (L); our pride in you (B); wrong to be proud of you (R)
decisions.reason: Book-wide choice: Literal keeps "boasting"; Balanced and Readable speak of pride, since this is good pride and the argument does not turn on the word itself.

decisions.choice: we would be put to shame for having been so confident, to say nothing of you
alternatives: we, not to say you, would be put to shame in this confidence
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps Paul's aside but moves it to the end, so the main clause reads without a break.

decisions.choice: And you will be even more ashamed!
decisions.reason: Readable says outright what Paul's aside implies (m5).

decisions.choice: nuestro motivo de gloria
decisions.reason: As in 1:14, the noun for boasting is "motivo de gloria" at Literal: what Paul has said with pride about the Corinthians, which could be shown to be empty.

source.text: ἀναγκαῖον οὖν ἡγησάμην παρακαλέσαι τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς ἵνα προέλθωσιν εἰς ὑμᾶς καὶ προκαταρτίσωσι τὴν προεπηγγελμένην εὐλογίαν ὑμῶν, ταύτην ἑτοίμην εἶναι οὕτως ὡς εὐλογίαν καὶ μὴ ὡς πλεονεξίαν.

records.literal_gloss: Necessary therefore I considered to urge the brothers that they go before to you and arrange beforehand the promised-beforehand blessing of you, this ready to be thus as blessing and not as greed.

en.L: Therefore I considered [it] necessary to urge the brothers to go ahead to you and to arrange in advance your blessing promised beforehand, [so that] this may be ready as a blessing and not as greed.
en.B: That is why I felt I had to ask the brothers to travel to you ahead of me and to put in order beforehand the generous gift you promised, so that it will be ready as a gift of generosity, not as a gift of greed.
en.R: So I thought I should ask these brothers to go to you before I come. They can help you get ready the gift you promised. Then it will be ready, and it will show that you are generous, not that you want to hold on to your money.

fr.L: J’ai donc estimé nécessaire d’exhorter les frères à aller d’avance chez vous et à préparer d’avance votre bénédiction promise d’avance, [afin] qu’elle soit ainsi prête comme une bénédiction et non comme de la cupidité.
fr.B: C’est pourquoi j’ai jugé nécessaire de demander aux frères de se rendre chez vous avant moi et d’organiser d’avance le don généreux que vous avez promis, pour qu’il soit prêt comme un don de la générosité et non de l’avarice.
fr.R: Alors j’ai pensé que je devais demander à ces frères d’aller chez vous avant que je vienne. Ils peuvent vous aider à préparer le don que vous avez promis. Ainsi, il sera prêt, et il montrera que vous êtes généreux, et non que vous voulez garder votre argent.

es.L: Por tanto, consideré necesario exhortar a los hermanos a que se adelantaran a ir a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y prepararan de antemano {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} bendición prometida de antemano, [para que] esta esté lista así, como bendición y no como avaricia.
es.B: Por eso me pareció necesario pedir a los hermanos que se adelantaran a {{plural_you:visitarlos|visitaros}} y dejaran organizada de antemano la ofrenda generosa que {{plural_you:prometieron|prometisteis}}, para que esté lista como fruto de la generosidad y no de la avaricia.
es.R: Por eso he pensado que debo pedir a estos hermanos que vayan a {{plural_you:verlos|veros}} antes de que yo llegue. Ellos pueden {{plural_you:ayudarlos|ayudaros}} a preparar la ofrenda que {{plural_you:prometieron|prometisteis}}. Así estará lista, y se verá que {{plural_you:son|sois}} generosos y que no {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} {{plural_you:aferrarse a su dinero|aferraros a vuestro dinero}}.

decisions.choice: blessing: a generous gift, which brings good to those who receive it
alternatives: blessing in the sense of words of praise
decisions.reason: εὐλογίαν means blessing, the good that is spoken over or given to someone. In the Greek Old Testament a gift sent to someone is sometimes called a blessing (Genesis 33:11; 1 Samuel 25:27), and Paul uses the word that way here. He plays on it: the gift is to be a real "blessing", and verse 6 speaks of sowing "with blessings".

decisions.choice: greed: a gift given grudgingly, by people who would rather keep what they have
alternatives: something extorted from the Corinthians by Paul
a gift given to get something back
decisions.reason: πλεονεξίαν is the craving to have more (Colossians 3:5). Set against "blessing", it most likely describes a gift given with a grasping spirit, squeezed out of givers who would rather hold on to their money. Some take it the other way, as something wrung out of the Corinthians by pressure; Paul may mean both: he sends the brothers ahead so that the gift does not have to be collected in a rush when he arrives (verse 4; 1 Corinthians 16:2).

decisions.choice: three words of "before": everything is to be done before Paul arrives
decisions.reason: Each of προέλθωσιν, προκαταρτίσωσι and προεπηγγελμένην begins with a prefix meaning "before": the brothers go ahead, they arrange it in advance, and the gift was promised in advance. Paul is anxious that the collection be finished before he comes with the Macedonians.

decisions.choice: blessing (L); generous gift, gift of generosity (B); gift, generous (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "blessing" so that the wordplay with verse 6 can be seen. In English "blessing" does not usually mean a gift of money, so Balanced and Readable say what is meant (m1).

decisions.choice: greed (L); a gift of greed (B); want to hold on to your money (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the contrast of generosity and greed in parallel phrases; Readable says what greed would look like in giving (m2).

decisions.choice: before I come
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the brothers go ahead of (m3).

decisions.choice: la cupidité (L); l’avarice (B)
decisions.reason: The greed meant here is holding on to what one has (m2), which French calls "avarice"; Literal keeps "cupidité", the general word for greed for gain.

decisions.choice: bendición (L); ofrenda generosa, fruto de la generosidad (B); la ofrenda, generosos (R)
decisions.reason: The blessing word here names a generous gift (meaning decision). Literal keeps "bendición" so the wordplay can be traced; Balanced and Readable say what is meant, as the English does.

source.text: Τοῦτο δέ, ὁ σπείρων φειδομένως φειδομένως καὶ θερίσει, καὶ ὁ σπείρων ἐπ’ εὐλογίαις ἐπ’ εὐλογίαις καὶ θερίσει.

records.literal_gloss: This and, the [one] sowing sparingly sparingly also will reap, and the [one] sowing upon blessings upon blessings also will reap.

en.L: Now [consider] this: the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows with blessings will also reap with blessings.
en.B: Keep this in mind: sow sparingly and you will reap sparingly; sow generously and you will reap generously.
en.R: Think about it this way. A farmer who plants only a few seeds will get only a small harvest. But a farmer who plants many seeds will get a big harvest.

fr.L: Or [considérez] ceci : celui qui sème chichement moissonnera aussi chichement, et celui qui sème avec bénédictions moissonnera aussi avec bénédictions.
fr.B: Retenez ceci : qui sème chichement moissonnera chichement ; qui sème généreusement moissonnera généreusement.
fr.R: Pensez-y de cette façon. Un fermier qui sème seulement quelques graines n’aura qu’une petite récolte. Mais un fermier qui sème beaucoup de graines aura une grosse récolte.

es.L: Y [{{plural_you:consideren|considerad}}] esto: el que siembra escasamente, escasamente también cosechará; y el que siembra con bendiciones, con bendiciones también cosechará.
es.B: {{plural_you:Tengan|Tened}} presente esto: el que siembra poco, poco cosechará; el que siembra con generosidad, con generosidad cosechará.
es.R: {{plural_you:Piénsenlo|Pensadlo}} así: un agricultor que siembra solo unas pocas semillas tendrá una cosecha pequeña. Pero un agricultor que siembra muchas semillas tendrá una gran cosecha.

decisions.choice: "this": a short way of saying "remember this" or "the point is this"
decisions.reason: Τοῦτο δέ has no verb. It points the reader to the saying that follows, as Paul does in 1 Corinthians 7:29 and 15:50.

decisions.choice: with blessings: generously, in abundance
decisions.reason: ἐπ εὐλογίαις means "on the basis of blessings": sowing in a way that is a blessing, that is, generously. Paul picks up the "blessing" of verse 5 and repeats it, as he repeats "sparingly": each kind of sowing brings back the same kind of harvest.

decisions.choice: the proverb of sowing and reaping
decisions.reason: Sowing and reaping was a familiar picture in Jewish wisdom: the generous person prospers (Proverbs 11:24-25), and the first line of Proverbs 22:8, whose Greek form Paul echoes in verse 7, says that one who sows wrong will reap trouble. Paul uses the same picture in Galatians 6:7-9.

decisions.choice: the harvest is God's generous provision, given so that they can keep giving
alternatives: a promise that giving money brings more money for oneself
decisions.reason: Paul does not promise wealth as a reward. Verses 8-11 explain the harvest: God makes every grace abound so that the givers have enough and can be generous in every good work, and the result is thanks to God.

decisions.choice: with blessings (L); generously (B); many seeds, a big harvest (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "blessings" so that the reader can see the link with verse 5 and the repetition in each half of the saying. Balanced keeps the repetition with "sparingly ... sparingly" and "generously ... generously".

decisions.choice: a farmer who plants
decisions.reason: Readable makes the farming picture explicit and leaves the reader to apply it to giving, as Paul does.

source.text: ἕκαστος καθὼς προῄρηται τῇ καρδίᾳ, μὴ ἐκ λύπης ἢ ἐξ ἀνάγκης· ἱλαρὸν γὰρ δότην ἀγαπᾷ ὁ θεός.

records.literal_gloss: Each just as he has decided in the heart, not out of grief or out of compulsion; cheerful for giver loves the God.

en.L: Each [one should give] just as {{gender:they have|he has}} decided in the heart, not out of grief or out of compulsion; for it is a cheerful giver God loves.
en.B: Each of you should give the amount you have settled on in your own heart, not with regret and not because you feel you must. God loves a giver who gives gladly.
en.R: Each of you should decide for yourself how much you will give. Do not be sad about giving, and do not give just because you feel you have to. God loves people who are happy to give.

fr.L: Chacun [doit donner] comme il l’a décidé dans le cœur, non par tristesse ni par contrainte ; car c’est un donateur joyeux que Dieu aime.
fr.B: Que chacun de vous donne le montant qu’il a fixé dans son cœur, non à regret ni par obligation. Dieu aime qui donne de bon cœur.
fr.R: Chacun de vous doit décider lui-même combien il va donner. Ne soyez pas tristes de donner, et ne donnez pas seulement parce que vous vous sentez obligés. Dieu aime les gens qui sont heureux de donner.

es.L: Cada uno [dé] según lo ha decidido en el corazón, no con tristeza ni por obligación; porque Dios ama al dador alegre.
es.B: Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe dar lo que haya decidido en su propio corazón, no con pesar ni porque se sienta obligado. Dios ama al que da con alegría.
es.R: Cada uno de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} debe decidir cuánto va a dar. No {{plural_you:den|deis}} con tristeza, ni {{plural_you:den|deis}} solo porque {{plural_you:se sienten|os sentís}} obligados. Dios ama a los que dan con alegría.

decisions.choice: "each should give": the verb is understood
decisions.reason: The sentence has no main verb; "give" is plain from the context. προῄρηται is a perfect: a decision made beforehand and settled, not made on the spot under pressure (verse 5).

decisions.choice: grief: regret at parting with the money; compulsion: pressure from others
decisions.reason: λύπης is grief or pain, here the pain of giving something up. ἀνάγκης is necessity or compulsion: giving because one is made to, or because others are watching. A gift given either way is not the "blessing" of verse 5.

decisions.choice: an echo of the Greek of Proverbs 22:8
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament adds a line to Proverbs 22:8 that is not in the Hebrew: God blesses a cheerful and giving man. Paul takes up the words "cheerful" and "giver" but says that God loves such a giver. The Greek puts "cheerful" first for emphasis.

decisions.choice: cheerful: glad, willing, giving with joy
decisions.reason: ἱλαρὸν describes a glad and willing spirit. Romans 12:8 uses the related noun of showing mercy with gladness. The point is the joy of giving freely, not a show of high spirits.

decisions.choice: each person, women and men
decisions.reason: ἕκαστος and the verb that goes with it are masculine singular, the ordinary way to speak of each member of a mixed group.

decisions.choice: {{gender:they have|he has}}
decisions.reason: Paul means every giver, women and men (m5). "He has" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: grief (L); regret (B); sad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering is "grief", which Literal keeps. Here the grief is regret over money given up (m2), and Balanced says so. Readable keeps the book-wide "sad".

decisions.choice: cheerful giver (L); a giver who gives gladly (B); people who are happy to give (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek order, with "cheerful" first for emphasis (m3). Balanced and Readable bring out that the gladness is in the giving itself (m4).

decisions.choice: "Chacun ... il l’a décidé", with no gender span (L)
decisions.reason: The English needs {{gender:they have|he has}} for the pronoun. French "chacun" already means every giver, women and men, and the "il" that refers back to it is ordinary generic French, so no span is used (style guide section 7).

decisions.choice: à regret (B); par tristesse (L); tristes (R)
decisions.reason: As in English, Balanced says what this grief is, regret at parting with the money (m2); Literal and Readable keep the grief family of chapter 7.

decisions.choice: lo ha decidido, with no gender setting
decisions.reason: The English Literal has a gender setting on its pronoun; the Spanish verb carries no pronoun, so "cada uno ... ha decidido" already includes women and men and needs no setting.

source.text: δυνατεῖ δὲ ὁ θεὸς πᾶσαν χάριν περισσεῦσαι εἰς ὑμᾶς, ἵνα ἐν παντὶ πάντοτε πᾶσαν αὐτάρκειαν ἔχοντες περισσεύητε εἰς πᾶν ἔργον ἀγαθόν·

records.literal_gloss: Is able and the God all grace to make abound to you, so that in everything always all sufficiency having you may abound for every work good;

en.L: And God is able to make all grace abound to you, so that, always having all sufficiency in everything, you may abound in every good work;
en.B: God is able to make all grace abound for you, so that in every way and at all times you will have everything you need, with plenty to spare for every good work.
en.R: God can give you every kind of grace, more than you need. Then you will always have all you need, and you will have plenty left over to share in every good thing you do.

fr.L: Et Dieu est capable de faire abonder pour vous toute grâce, afin qu’ayant toujours, en toutes choses, tout ce qui suffit, vous abondiez pour toute œuvre bonne ;
fr.B: Dieu a le pouvoir de faire abonder pour vous toute grâce, pour qu’en toutes choses et en tout temps vous ayez tout ce qu’il vous faut, et qu’il vous en reste en abondance pour toute œuvre bonne.
fr.R: Dieu peut vous donner toutes sortes de grâces, plus que ce dont vous avez besoin. Alors vous aurez toujours tout ce qu’il vous faut, et il vous en restera beaucoup à partager pour tout ce que vous faites de bien.

es.L: Y poderoso es Dios para hacer abundar toda gracia para con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, a fin de que, teniendo siempre en todo toda suficiencia, {{plural_you:abunden|abundéis}} para toda buena obra;
es.B: Dios puede hacer que toda gracia abunde para {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, de modo que en todo y en todo momento {{plural_you:tengan|tengáis}} todo lo necesario, y aun {{plural_you:les|os}} sobre para toda buena obra.
es.R: Dios puede {{plural_you:darles|daros}} toda clase de gracia, más de la que {{plural_you:necesitan|necesitáis}}. Así siempre {{plural_you:tendrán|tendréis}} todo lo necesario, y {{plural_you:les|os}} sobrará para compartir en todo lo bueno que {{plural_you:hagan|hagáis}}.

decisions.choice: all grace: every kind of God's generous favor, including what they need in order to give
decisions.reason: πᾶσαν χάριν is the grace of God that runs through chapters 8-9: the grace that moved the Macedonians to give (8:1) and the grace of Christ who became poor (8:9). Here it takes in the material means to give as well; the next clause speaks of having enough. God is the sower's supplier (verse 10), and his grace is the harvest of verse 6.

decisions.choice: sufficiency: having enough of what one needs
decisions.reason: αὐτάρκειαν was a favorite word of Stoic teachers for the wise person who needs nothing from outside himself. Paul uses the word but not the idea of self-reliance: the enough comes from God, as in Philippians 4:11-13.

decisions.choice: "all ... every ... always ... all ... every": Paul piles up words of fullness
decisions.reason: The sentence repeats the word for "all" four times and adds "always", and it uses the verb "abound" twice. The fullness of God's giving is the point: God gives in full so that they can give freely.

decisions.choice: the purpose of God's abundance: so that they can give in every good work
alternatives: so that they may be rich
decisions.reason: ἵνα gives the purpose. They are to have enough so that they can overflow in good works, and here the good work in view is generous giving, such as the collection.

decisions.choice: abound; with plenty to spare
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps "abound" for God's grace and says what the second "abound" means for the givers: more than enough to give.

decisions.choice: to share
decisions.reason: Readable says what the overflow is for (m4).

source.text: καθὼς γέγραπται· Ἐσκόρπισεν, ἔδωκεν τοῖς πένησιν, ἡ δικαιοσύνη αὐτοῦ μένει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα·

records.literal_gloss: Just as it has been written, He scattered, he gave to the poor, the righteousness of him remains into the age;

en.L: as it is written, "He scattered, he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever."
en.B: As it is written: "He has scattered his gifts far and wide and given to people in need; his righteousness lasts forever."
en.R: The Scriptures say this about people who honor God: "They give freely to the poor. Their righteousness will last forever."

fr.L: selon qu’il est écrit : « Il a dispersé, il a donné aux pauvres ; sa justice demeure pour toujours. »
fr.B: Comme il est écrit : « Il a répandu ses dons de tous côtés, il a donné aux personnes dans le besoin ; sa justice dure à jamais. »
fr.R: Les Écritures disent ceci au sujet des gens qui honorent Dieu : « Ils donnent généreusement aux pauvres. Leur justice durera toujours. »

es.L: como está escrito: «Esparció, dio a los pobres; su justicia permanece para siempre».
es.B: Como está escrito: «Ha repartido sus dones a manos llenas, ha dado a los necesitados; su justicia permanece para siempre».
es.R: Las Escrituras dicen esto acerca de los que honran a Dios: «Dan con generosidad a los pobres. Su justicia durará para siempre».

decisions.choice: a quotation of Psalm 112:9
decisions.reason: Paul quotes the Greek of Psalm 112:9 (111:9 in the Greek numbering) word for word. The psalm describes the person who fears the LORD (the divine name stands in the Hebrew of verse 1): such a person is generous, lends freely and gives to the poor.

decisions.choice: the subject is the generous person of the psalm
alternatives: God, who scatters his gifts and whose righteousness lasts forever
decisions.reason: In Psalm 112 the subject is the person who fears the LORD, and Paul is speaking about the Corinthians' giving. Some take God as the subject here, since verse 8 has just spoken of what God is able to do and Psalm 111:3 says the same words about God. Either way the givers' righteousness is God's work in them.

decisions.choice: righteousness: right living, here shown in generous giving to the poor
decisions.reason: δικαιοσύνη in this psalm is the faithful, upright conduct of a person who lives as God wants, which shows itself in care for the poor. In later Jewish usage the word could even mean gifts to the poor (compare Matthew 6:1-2). Here it is the goodness of the giver, which God remembers and which lasts.

decisions.choice: scattered: gave freely and widely, like a sower scattering seed
decisions.reason: Ἐσκόρπισεν is to scatter or spread abroad. It fits the sowing picture of verses 6 and 10: the generous person scatters gifts as a sower scatters seed. πένησιν are poor people who must work to live.

decisions.choice: forever
decisions.reason: εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα means "into the age", the ordinary Greek way of saying "forever".

decisions.choice: he, his
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep the singular of the psalm, which speaks of one representative person; it is the figure of the psalm, not God, so the pronouns take no deity_pronoun span (m2).

decisions.choice: about people who honor God: "They give freely ... Their righteousness"
alternatives: He scattered, he gave to the poor; his righteousness remains forever
decisions.reason: Readable says whom the psalm describes (m1) and uses the plural, since the psalm's person stands for anyone who fears God. It follows the main reading of the subject (m2).

decisions.choice: his gifts far and wide
decisions.reason: Balanced says what was scattered (m4).

decisions.choice: la justice (every level)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for righteousness, kept at Readable too, as the English keeps "righteousness"; here it is right living shown in giving (m3), and "donner aux pauvres" beside it makes that plain.

decisions.choice: su justicia, with no deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: In the psalm the one who scatters and gives is the generous person (meaning decision), not God, so "su" takes no deity_pronoun setting, as the English "his" takes none.

source.text: ὁ δὲ ἐπιχορηγῶν σπόρον τῷ σπείροντι καὶ ἄρτον εἰς βρῶσιν χορηγήσει καὶ πληθυνεῖ τὸν σπόρον ὑμῶν καὶ αὐξήσει τὰ γενήματα τῆς δικαιοσύνης ὑμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: The [one] and supplying seed to the [one] sowing and bread for eating will supply and will multiply the seed of you and will increase the produce of the righteousness of you;

en.L: And the one who provides seed for the sower and bread for eating will provide and multiply your seed and will make the yield of your righteousness grow;
en.B: God, who provides seed for the sower and bread to eat, will provide you with seed as well, and multiply it, and make your righteousness yield a bigger harvest.
en.R: God gives seed to farmers to plant, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gives bread for people to eat. In the same way, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will give you all the seed you need, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will make it multiply. Then your righteousness will produce a great harvest.

fr.L: Or celui qui fournit la semence au semeur et du pain pour la nourriture fournira et multipliera votre semence et fera croître les fruits de votre justice ;
fr.B: Dieu, qui fournit la semence au semeur et le pain pour se nourrir, vous fournira à vous aussi de la semence, la multipliera, et fera produire à votre justice une plus grande récolte.
fr.R: Dieu donne aux fermiers des graines à semer, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} donne du pain pour que les gens mangent. De la même façon, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} vous donnera toutes les graines dont vous avez besoin, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les fera se multiplier. Alors votre justice produira une grande récolte.

es.L: Y el que provee semilla al que siembra y pan para comer proveerá y multiplicará la semilla de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y hará crecer los frutos de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} justicia;
es.B: Dios, que da semilla al que siembra y pan para comer, también {{plural_you:les|os}} dará semilla a {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y la multiplicará, y hará que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} justicia produzca una cosecha mayor.
es.R: Dios da semilla a los agricultores para que siembren, y da pan a la gente para que coma. Del mismo modo, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} {{plural_you:les|os}} dará toda la semilla que {{plural_you:necesiten|necesitéis}} y hará que se multiplique. Entonces la justicia de {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} producirá una gran cosecha.

decisions.choice: echoes of Isaiah 55:10 and Hosea 10:12
decisions.reason: "Seed to the sower and bread for food" are the words of the Greek of Isaiah 55:10, where the rain and snow make the earth give seed and bread, as God's word does what he sends it to do. "The produce of your righteousness" echoes the Greek of Hosea 10:12, a call to sow righteousness and reap its fruit.

decisions.choice: the one who provides is God
decisions.reason: The participle has no named subject, but the words of Isaiah 55:10 and verse 8 make it plain that God is meant.

decisions.choice: bread for eating goes with "the one who provides", as in Isaiah 55:10
alternatives: "will provide bread for food": the bread goes with the promise
decisions.reason: The Greek can be read either way, but Isaiah 55:10 joins seed for the sower and bread for food, and Paul follows those words. The promise is then about the Corinthians' seed: God will give them more to sow.

decisions.choice: follow SBLGNT: promises, "he will provide ... multiply ... make grow"
alternatives: later manuscripts have wishes: "may he provide ... multiply ... make grow"
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, have the three verbs as wishes or prayers instead of promises. The difference is one or two letters in each verb. The older manuscripts have the future, as SBLGNT does. Reviewers must check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: your seed: what they have to give; the harvest of righteousness: the good their giving produces
decisions.reason: Paul applies the picture: God gives the Corinthians the means to give, makes it more, and makes the right living shown in their generosity (verse 9) bear fruit, which verses 11-14 describe as thanks to God.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name God (m2). Readable's pronouns for him follow the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: In the same way ... all the seed you need
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the promise applies the picture from Isaiah to the Corinthians (m5).

source.text: ἐν παντὶ πλουτιζόμενοι εἰς πᾶσαν ἁπλότητα, ἥτις κατεργάζεται δι’ ἡμῶν εὐχαριστίαν τῷ θεῷ ὅτι ἡ διακονία τῆς λειτουργίας ταύτης οὐ μόνον ἐστὶν προσαναπληροῦσα τὰ ὑστερήματα τῶν ἁγίων, ἀλλὰ καὶ περισσεύουσα διὰ πολλῶν εὐχαριστιῶν τῷ θεῷ διὰ τῆς δοκιμῆς τῆς διακονίας ταύτης δοξάζοντες τὸν θεὸν ἐπὶ τῇ ὑποταγῇ τῆς ὁμολογίας ὑμῶν εἰς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τοῦ Χριστοῦ καὶ ἁπλότητι τῆς κοινωνίας εἰς αὐτοὺς καὶ εἰς πάντας, καὶ αὐτῶν δεήσει ὑπὲρ ὑμῶν ἐπιποθούντων ὑμᾶς διὰ τὴν ὑπερβάλλουσαν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ ἐφ’ ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: In everything being enriched for all generosity, which produces through us thanksgiving to the God, \v 12 because the ministry of the service this not only is filling up the needs of the holy ones, but also overflowing through many thanksgivings to the God, \v 13 through the proof of the ministry this glorifying the God upon the submission of the confession of you to the gospel of the Christ and generosity of the sharing toward them and toward all, \v 14 and of them with prayer for you longing for you because of the surpassing grace of the God upon you.

en.L: [You will be] enriched in everything for all generosity, which produces thanksgiving to God through us; \v 12 for the ministry of this service is not only filling up the needs of the holy ones, but is also overflowing through many thanksgivings to God; \v 13 through the proof of this ministry [they will be] glorifying God for the submission of your confession to the gospel of the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} and for the generosity of [your] sharing with them and with all, \v 14 and [by] their prayer for you, [as they are] longing for you because of the surpassing grace of God upon you.
en.B: You will be made rich in every way so that you can be generous in every way, and your generosity, carried by us, will bring about thanksgiving to God. \v 12 For this relief, a sacred service, not only fills up what God's holy people lack; it also overflows in many thanksgivings to God. \v 13 This relief will show what you are, and they will give glory to God for it: for the way you submit to the gospel of {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} that you confess, and for the generosity of your partnership with them and with everyone. \v 14 And when they pray for you, they will long for you, because of the surpassing grace of God that rests on you.
en.R: God will make you rich in every way, so that you can always give generously. Then, when we take your gift to God's people, they will thank God for it. \v 12 This helping is a service to God, like the work of a priest. It gives God's people what they need. But it does more than that. It makes many people thank God. \v 13 The help you give will prove that your faith is real. So they will give glory to God, because you obey the good news about {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} that you openly confess, and because you share so generously with them and with everyone. \v 14 They will pray for you, and they will long to see you, because God's grace to you is so great.

fr.L: [Vous serez] enrichis en tout pour toute générosité, qui produit par nous l’action de grâce envers Dieu ; \v 12 car le ministère de ce service non seulement comble les besoins des saints, mais déborde aussi par de nombreuses actions de grâce envers Dieu ; \v 13 par la preuve [que donne] ce ministère, [ils] glorifieront Dieu pour la soumission de votre confession à l’Évangile du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} et pour la générosité de [votre] partage avec eux et avec tous, \v 14 et [par] leur prière pour vous, [eux qui] vous désirent ardemment à cause de la grâce surabondante de Dieu sur vous.
fr.B: Vous serez enrichis de toutes les manières pour pouvoir être généreux de toutes les manières, et votre générosité, que nous porterons, fera monter vers Dieu l’action de grâce. \v 12 Car ce secours, qui est un service sacré, ne comble pas seulement ce qui manque au peuple saint de Dieu ; il déborde aussi en de nombreuses actions de grâce envers Dieu. \v 13 Ce secours montrera ce que vous êtes, et ils en rendront gloire à Dieu : pour la manière dont vous vous soumettez à l’Évangile du {{christos:Christ|Messie}} que vous confessez, et pour la générosité avec laquelle vous êtes solidaires d’eux et de tous. \v 14 Et quand ils prieront pour vous, ils auront un vif désir de vous voir, à cause de la grâce extraordinaire de Dieu qui repose sur vous.
fr.R: Dieu vous rendra riches de toutes les manières, pour que vous puissiez toujours donner généreusement. Alors, quand nous apporterons votre don au peuple de Dieu, ils remercieront Dieu pour cela. \v 12 Cette aide est un service pour Dieu, comme le travail d’un prêtre. Elle donne au peuple de Dieu ce dont il a besoin. Mais elle fait plus que cela. Elle pousse beaucoup de gens à remercier Dieu. \v 13 L’aide que vous donnez prouvera que votre foi est vraie. Alors ils rendront gloire à Dieu, parce que vous obéissez à la bonne nouvelle au sujet du {{christos:Christ|Messie}}, que vous reconnaissez ouvertement, et parce que vous partagez si généreusement avec eux et avec tout le monde. \v 14 Ils prieront pour vous, et ils désireront vous voir, parce que la grâce que Dieu vous a donnée est si grande.

es.L: [{{plural_you:Serán|Seréis}}] enriquecidos en todo para toda generosidad, la cual produce por medio de nosotros acción de gracias a Dios; \v 12 porque el ministerio de este servicio no solo suple las necesidades de los santos, sino que también abunda en muchas acciones de gracias a Dios; \v 13 por la prueba de este ministerio [ellos estarán] glorificando a Dios por la sumisión de {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} confesión al evangelio del {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}} y por la generosidad de [{{plural_you:su|vuestra}}] comunión con ellos y con todos, \v 14 y [por] la oración de ellos por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, [mientras] {{plural_you:los|os}} añoran a causa de la sobreabundante gracia de Dios sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.B: {{plural_you:Serán|Seréis}} enriquecidos en todo para que {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} ser generosos en todo, y esa generosidad, llevada por nosotros, hará que se den gracias a Dios. \v 12 Porque esta ayuda, que es un servicio sagrado, no solo cubre lo que le falta al pueblo santo de Dios, sino que también rebosa en muchas acciones de gracias a Dios. \v 13 Esta ayuda mostrará lo que {{plural_you:ustedes son|vosotros sois}}, y por ella darán gloria a Dios: por la obediencia con que {{plural_you:se someten|os sometéis}} al evangelio {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} que {{plural_you:confiesan|confesáis}}, y por la generosidad con que {{plural_you:comparten|compartís}} con ellos y con todos. \v 14 Y cuando oren por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, {{plural_you:los|os}} añorarán, por la extraordinaria gracia de Dios que está sobre {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Dios {{plural_you:los|os}} hará ricos en todo, para que siempre {{plural_you:puedan|podáis}} dar con generosidad. Entonces, cuando llevemos {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} ofrenda al pueblo de Dios, ellos darán gracias a Dios por ella. \v 12 Esta ayuda es un servicio a Dios, como el trabajo de un sacerdote. Da al pueblo de Dios lo que necesita. Pero hace más que eso: hace que mucha gente dé gracias a Dios. \v 13 La ayuda que {{plural_you:ustedes dan|vosotros dais}} demostrará que {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} fe es auténtica. Por eso darán gloria a Dios, porque {{plural_you:ustedes obedecen|vosotros obedecéis}} la buena noticia acerca {{christos:de Cristo|del Mesías}} que {{plural_you:confiesan|confesáis}} abiertamente, y porque {{plural_you:comparten|compartís}} con tanta generosidad con ellos y con todos. \v 14 Orarán por {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} y desearán mucho {{plural_you:verlos|veros}}, porque la gracia de Dios para con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} es muy grande.

decisions.choice: "being enriched": a loose participle that carries on the promise of verse 8
decisions.reason: πλουτιζόμενοι has no main verb to hang on. It most naturally goes back to "you" in verse 8, with verses 9-10 as an aside: God will make them rich in every way. The riches are for generosity, not for keeping, as in 8:9.

decisions.choice: generosity: wholehearted, open-handed giving
decisions.reason: As in 8:2, ἁπλότητα is singleness of heart that gives without holding back or calculating. It comes again in verse 13.

decisions.choice: through us: through Paul and those who carry the gift to Jerusalem
decisions.reason: δι ἡμῶν means that Paul's part in collecting and delivering the gift (8:19-20) is the channel through which the Corinthians' generosity becomes thanks to God from the believers in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: the collection for the poor believers in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: διακονία and διακονίας are the relief fund, as in verse 1 and 8:4. "The holy ones" are the believers in Jerusalem (Romans 15:25-26).

decisions.choice: service: a service done for the community and offered to God, with a priestly overtone
decisions.reason: λειτουργίας was used for public services that a citizen paid for, and in the Greek Old Testament for the priests' service in the tabernacle and temple. Paul uses the word family of the Philippians' gift (Philippians 2:17, 25, 30) and of Gentiles sharing material help with Jerusalem (Romans 15:27). The collection is practical help, but it is also an offering made to God, and it ends in worship.

decisions.choice: proof: what the relief shows the Corinthians to be
alternatives: a test still to be passed
decisions.reason: δοκιμῆς is the quality that testing brings to light, as in 2:9 and 8:2. The relief proves that their love and faith are genuine (8:8, 24).

decisions.choice: the subject of "glorifying": the believers in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: δοξάζοντες is another loose participle. Those who give glory to God are the holy ones whose needs are met (verse 12), who will pray for the Corinthians (verse 14).

decisions.choice: the obedience that goes with confessing the gospel of Christ
decisions.reason: ὑποταγῇ is submission or obedience, and ὁμολογίας the confession or open declaration of faith. The phrase means that their obedience matches what they confess: they acknowledge the gospel of Christ and live it out by giving. The Jerusalem believers will see that the Gentile churches' faith is real.

decisions.choice: the collection binds Gentile and Jewish believers together
decisions.reason: κοινωνίας is the partnership word of 8:4 and Philippians 1:5: sharing in a common life and work. Paul hoped the gift would show the believers in Jerusalem that the Gentile churches belonged with them (Romans 15:25-31). "With all" widens the partnership beyond Jerusalem to all believers, or to all people.

decisions.choice: their prayer and longing are the Jerusalem believers' response
alternatives: Jerusalem's prayer is a second ground of thanks to God
decisions.reason: The words are loosely joined to what goes before, most likely as a further result: the receivers will not only praise God but pray for the givers and long for them. Gift and prayer flow in both directions.

decisions.choice: the surpassing grace of God in the Corinthians: the passage ends where it began
decisions.reason: χάριν is God's grace, as in 8:1, where it was given to the Macedonians. Now the believers in Jerusalem will see the same grace at work in the Corinthians. ὑπερβάλλουσαν means going beyond measure (3:10).

decisions.choice: ministry (L); relief (B); helping, help (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide choice for the collection, as in verse 1 and 8:4 (m4).

decisions.choice: service (L); a sacred service (B); a service to God, like the work of a priest (R)
decisions.reason: Literal says "service". Balanced adds "sacred" and Readable compares it with a priest's work, so that the reader hears the overtone of worship in the word (m5).

decisions.choice: holy ones (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering of this word.

decisions.choice: {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} (L); {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} (B, R)
decisions.reason: Title setting. Literal keeps the article.

decisions.choice: submission of your confession to the gospel (L); the way you submit to the gospel ... that you confess (B); you obey the good news ... that you openly confess (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Greek phrase; Balanced and Readable say how obedience and confession belong together (m8).

decisions.choice: sharing (L); partnership (B); share (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses "partnership", the word chosen for this noun in 8:4 and in Philippians (m9).

decisions.choice: when we take your gift to God's people, they will thank God; prove that your faith is real
alternatives: through us thanksgiving to God; the proof
decisions.reason: Readable says how the thanks comes about (m3) and what the proof shows (m6).

decisions.choice: carried by us
decisions.reason: Balanced says how Paul's part makes the gift into thanks (m3).

decisions.choice: l’action de grâce, les actions de grâce (L, B); remercier (R)
decisions.reason: "Action de grâce" is the ordinary French phrase for thanks given to God, and it lets the reader hear the grace of verses 8 and 14 in the thanks it produces, as Paul's Greek does. Readable uses the everyday verb.

decisions.choice: [votre] partage (L); vous êtes solidaires (B)
decisions.reason: "Communion" would suggest the Lord's Supper to many readers, and "partenariat" is business language; Literal says "partage", as the English says "sharing", and Balanced gives the sense of the English "partnership" (m9) with "solidaires".

decisions.choice: comunión (L); la generosidad con que comparten (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "comunión", the traditional word for a shared life and a shared work; Balanced and Readable say plainly what the sharing is here, giving to the believers in Jerusalem (meaning decision).

decisions.choice: [mientras] los añoran
decisions.reason: The Greek participle "longing for you" cannot take a ustedes/vosotros setting as one Spanish word, so Literal writes it as a clause with a supplied "mientras".

source.text: χάρις τῷ θεῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἀνεκδιηγήτῳ αὐτοῦ δωρεᾷ.

records.literal_gloss: Thanks to the God for the indescribable of him gift.

en.L: Thanks [be] to God for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} gift that cannot be told in full.
en.B: Thanks be to God for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} gift, which no words can describe!
en.R: We thank God for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} gift. It is too wonderful for words!

fr.L: Grâce [soit rendue] à Dieu pour {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} don qu’on ne peut pas décrire entièrement.
fr.B: Grâce soit rendue à Dieu pour {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} don, qu’aucune parole ne peut décrire !
fr.R: Nous remercions Dieu pour {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} don. Ce don est plus merveilleux que tout ce que les mots peuvent dire !

es.L: Gracias [sean] a Dios por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} don indescriptible.
es.B: ¡Gracias a Dios por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} don, que no hay palabras para describir!
es.R: Damos gracias a Dios por {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} regalo. ¡Es tan maravilloso que no hay palabras para describirlo!

decisions.choice: thanks: gratitude given to God
decisions.reason: χάρις with "to God" and no verb is the set phrase for giving thanks, as in 2:14 and 8:16. It closes Paul's play on the word through chapters 8-9: the grace God gives (8:1; 9:8, 14) produces generous gifts and returns to him as thanks.

decisions.choice: God's gift: his gift of himself in Christ, from which all this giving flows
alternatives: the grace at work in the collection and the unity it brings
decisions.reason: δωρεᾷ is a free gift. Paul most likely means the gift of Christ, who became poor so that they might become rich (8:9), the source of all the grace in these chapters. Some take it as the grace shown in the collection itself and the bond it makes between Gentile and Jewish believers; the two belong together.

decisions.choice: beyond description: more than words can fully tell
decisions.reason: ἀνεκδιηγήτῳ means that cannot be told through to the end. Paul runs out of words for what God has given.

decisions.choice: Thanks (L, B); We thank (R)
decisions.reason: The key term is rendered "thanks" here because the sense is gratitude (m1), as in 2:14 and 8:16.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}
decisions.reason: The pronoun for God follows the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: that cannot be told in full (L); which no words can describe (B); too wonderful for words (R)
decisions.reason: Each level says what the Greek word says (m3) in plain words. "Unspeakable" in older English now suggests something too bad to mention.

decisions.choice: Grâce [soit rendue] à Dieu (L); Grâce soit rendue à Dieu (B); Nous remercions Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:16: French keeps the key word "grâce" in its idiom of thanks at Literal and Balanced, so the chapters on the gift of grace end on the same word.

decisions.choice: gracias
decisions.reason: As in 2:14 and 8:16, the grace word here means thanks to God, which Spanish says with its plural "gracias", the same root.
